claim_text: gc.bigPackThreshold is ignored when the number of kept packs exceeds gc.autoPackLimit.
gc.bigPackThreshold defaults to 1 GB.
must-revalidate binds every cache.
A server that wants every request validated can assign an expiration time in the past.
Running git pack-refs makes a repository unclonable over dumb transports by Git versions before 1.5.1.2.
If a response has both max-age and Expires, the recipient must ignore Expires.
Deleting such an object can make the other process fail or corrupt the repository if it later adds a reference to it.
git gc keeps objects referenced by branches, tags, the index, remote-tracking branches and reflogs.
An object referenced only by a git note is kept alive by git gc.
Git stores loose objects zlib-compressed under .git/objects.
By default git gc calls git worktree prune --expire 3.weeks.ago.
Reflog entries expire after 90 days by default.
HTTP freshness is primarily determined by explicit expiration times that the origin assigns with Expires or max-age.
If gc.log exists, git gc --auto prints its content instead of running.
Historically, Expires could be no more than a year in the future.
The presence of an Age header implies the origin did not generate or validate the response for this request.
The stale-while-revalidate extension lets caches serve stale content while they revalidate in the background.
Most CDNs cap freshness lifetimes at one week.
gc.logExpiry defaults to one day.
Setting gc.pruneExpire to "never" suppresses pruning.
A shared cache may reuse a cached response to a request with an Authorization header whenever the response is fresh.
By default git gc --auto returns immediately and runs in the background when the system supports it.
--prune=now is the safest choice when another process is writing to the repository concurrently.
If two suitable responses are stored, a cache uses the one with the earlier Date header.
A disconnected cache that cannot revalidate a must-revalidate response should return 502 (Bad Gateway).
The unqualified private directive allows shared caches to store the response.
git gc --auto packs loose objects once there are roughly more than 6700 of them.
GitHub runs git gc on hosted repositories automatically.
RFC 7234 formally deprecated the Pragma header.
If several suitable responses are stored, the cache must use the oldest one.
The Expires header does not imply that the resource will change at that time.
git gc --auto consolidates packs once there are more than 50 packs not marked with a .keep file.
gc.autoPackLimit defaults to 50 packs not marked with a .keep file, past which packs are consolidated into one larger pack.
HTTP/2 transmits Age as a pseudo-header.
A cache may invalidate URIs from the Location header even when their origin differs from the target URI's.
Setting gc.auto to 0 leaves the gc.autoPackLimit heuristic active.
gc.autoDetach defaults to true.
A disconnected cache may serve a stale response even if it carries must-revalidate.
A client sending max-age=0 without max-stale is asking not to receive a stale response.
Since Git 2.29, automatic housekeeping is increasingly handled by git maintenance.
